title: Chapter 88
content:
Sob... Uuuugh...

Curled into a massive, pathetic ball on the narrow hospital cot, Wang Ryun was weeping his eyes out.

The moment he came to from the knockout, he hadn't even looked at the two brothers who saved his life, immediately demanding to know if his beloved had truly sold him out. Having worried about how to break the news, Jakyeong figured getting it over with was for the best.

Never having loved anyone to the point of tears, Jakyeong couldn't fathom the theatrics. Han, possessing a bit more romantic history, gently peeled back the blanket to console him.

"Stop crying, Ryun... We'll track her down."

Han cut his eyes toward Jakyeong, gesturing frantically: Comfort him. Say something.

Jakyeong let out a dry sigh, giving Ryun’s trembling shoulder a stiff pat.

"If you want... I can put a bullet in her for you."

Han swatted Jakyeong’s arm, but Jakyeong pressed on:

"Since you're my brother, I won't even charge you. Free contract."

Ryun whipped the duvet off, bolting upright. A dark purple knot was blooming across his jaw where Jakyeong had kicked him, paired with a bloody tissue shoved up one nostril. Ripping the sodden paper from his nose, he glared daggers at Jakyeong—tears and snot streaming down his face in equal measure.

Jakyeong felt a pang of pity, but a treacherous snort threatened to escape his throat.

Fuck. Don't laugh. Laugh now and he'll actually try to kill me.

"Wei! You don't know the first thing about love! That's why you spew such idiotic bullshit!"

Why am I catching strays? Jakyeong looked to Han for backup, but Han offered none. Seeing Ryun genuinely shattered, a sliver of guilt crept in. Reaching out to pull the blanket over his brother, Ryun slapped his hand away and flopped back down.

Jakyeong leaned in, giving his shoulder a gentle squeeze. "I'm sorry, Ryun-ge... I didn't mean it like that."

Ryun pulled the covers over his head, refusing to move. Han and Jakyeong exchanged helpless sighs. An IV drip containing fresh sedatives was slowly trickling into Ryun’s forearm.

When the muffled wailing persisted, Jakyeong stepped into the corridor, asking the charge nurse if they could max out the dosage. When she confirmed he was already at the human ceiling, Jakyeong politely asked if they had veterinary tranquilizers rated for bears or bulls, earning an immediate, frosty dismissal.

They waited in silence until the sobbing and cursing tapered off. Han lifted the corner of the duvet: Ryun was fast asleep, snoring like a chainsaw through a tear-stained face. Han tucked him in properly with a quiet, sorrowful look.

Stepping into the hall, they nodded to the security detail and headed down to the outdoor smoking shelter to burn through several cigarettes. Consoling the heartbroken is grueling work.

Han’s phone buzzed. Expecting the fugitive ex-girlfriend, he answered an unknown number. The voice on the line made Han’s posture instantly stiffen. Glancing at Jakyeong, he switched to rapid-fire Mandarin, stepping out of the shelter.

Finishing his smoke, Jakyeong followed him out. Han was just hanging up.

"Who was that?"

Han let out a slow, troubled breath. "Jun. Sounds like he's in Seoul."

Jakyeong paused, blinking. "Who?"

"Your old instructor. Takeya Jun."

Jakyeong’s brow pinched.

The name belonged to a Japanese expatriate who had lived in their district during Jakyeong's childhood in Macau. Young Jakyeong had run errands for him for pocket money, and the man was the one who had practically taught him how to handle a firearm.

When Jakyeong grew older, he learned the man was a contract killer and naturally absorbed the trade. But their partnership didn't last—fracturing permanently the day Jakyeong walked in on him about to execute a child.

They parted ways with bad blood. Jun had sneered that Jakyeong had too soft a heart to ever survive as a proper assassin, yet Jakyeong was still putting food on the table with a gun. The man occasionally checked in with Wang Han, though even those calls had dried up in recent years, fueling rumors that he had caught a bullet.

"So the bastard is still breathing."

"Arrived in Korea yesterday."

"Why the hell is he in Seoul?"

"A contract, most likely." Han sighed. "He asked where we were based, but I gave him a vague brush-off. He asked about you, too."

Jakyeong stayed quiet. There was zero love lost between them. He had learned marksmanship from the man, but he refused to view him as human. Outsiders might lump all contract killers together as identical filth, but to Jakyeong, Jun belonged to a breed of vermin far worse than garbage.

They walked to the parking garage. As Jakyeong pulled the sedan into traffic, Il-hyun’s surveillance detail locked onto their rear bumper. Having abandoned all subtlety, they trailed openly like an official motorcade.

Cruising through the city, Jakyeong remembered the earlier conversation.

"Han-ge."

Han looked over from the passenger window. "Yeah?"

"President Kang and I talked in my room earlier."

"I saw," Han deadpanned. "Looked like a very passionate discussion."

Jakyeong ground his teeth. Swore he wouldn't say a word, and here he is poking at it. When Jakyeong threw a playful jab, Han ducked with a chuckle. Jakyeong quickly steered the subject back, relaying Il-hyun’s proposal to ship them off to a private estate in Hawaii for a month.

Han’s eyes widened. "Out of nowhere?"

"Ryun-ge took a blade, and my arm is stitched up..."

"Strange. He doesn't strike me as the delicate type to worry over minor scrapes." Han paused, studying Jakyeong's profile. "Is this because of you?"

Just as Han suspected, Il-hyun was terrified Jakyeong would be used as leverage against him. Idiot. If you invest an obscene fortune in an asset, you put it to work. If you were just going to bubble-wrap me, why hire us in the first place? Being treated like fragile glass rubbed his pride raw.

"So? Did you accept?"

"Not yet."

Han turned it over in his head. "Ryun is in rough shape anyway. Going overseas to lay low and recover isn't the worst play."

Logically, it made sense, yet an irritating knot pulled at Jakyeong’s chest. Tactically speaking, wasn't this the exact moment Il-hyun needed maximum firepower around him? Or did the man think that while the trio excelled at wet-work, they were useless as bodyguards? With Park Tae-soo and a small army of seasoned operatives on payroll, it was a fair assessment.

So why do I feel so damn bitter about it...?

I can protect you just fine.

The unbidden thought struck him like a physical blow.

In a moment of sheer panic, Jakyeong slammed both feet onto the brakes.

SCREECH—!

The pursuit sedan behind them locked its tires, blaring its horn in frantic protest. Han was thrown forward, catching the dashboard with a startled yelp.

"What the hell, Wei?!"

Jakyeong signaled a quick apology to the car behind them and eased back onto the gas, his mind reeling. Have I lost my mind? Protect who?

He was letting his thoughts run completely off the rails. He needed to worry about protecting his own aching backside from that degenerate, not playing bodyguard to a billionaire sociopath. Even now, every bump in the asphalt sent a dull throb straight to his tailbone.

Leaving the urban sprawl behind, the car wound into the secluded countryside surrounding the estate. The terrain was dead flat—Il-hyun had leveled the surrounding knolls to deny snipers an angle of approach.

Rounding the bend, an unfamiliar black sedan was parked near the gates, flanked by a small refrigerated transport truck.

Inside the perimeter, the property was eerily quiet. The gate sentries were nowhere to be seen, leaving only the chirping of crickets in the grass.

Stepping out into the drive, heavy footsteps brushed through the lawn from the rear gardens.

Jakyeong went on guard, then froze.

Emerging from the shadows was Kang Il-hyun—his white dress shirt and handsome face completely drenched in fresh, scarlet blood, looking like a demon pulled straight from the pit.

He struck a flame to his cigarette, pausing when his eyes met Jakyeong's. To anyone else, the visual would have induced a heart attack.

Exhaling a cloud of gray smoke, Il-hyun offered a calm, effortless smile.

"Back already, darling? How's Ryun holding up?"

Jakyeong opened his mouth, speechless. I'm the one who should be asking if you're alright.

Il-hyun dragged the back of his hand across his cheek, smearing the crimson deeper into his skin and making the sight twice as terrifying.

Moments later, two unfamiliar operatives emerged from the side path, hauling a heavy wooden freight crate toward the refrigerated truck. Judging by the dimensions, it carried a human corpse.

"Who was that?" Jakyeong asked.

"Let's head inside first."

Il-hyun led the way, with Jakyeong and Han trailing behind. Jakyeong glanced over his shoulder just in time to see the operatives slam the truck doors shut and speed through the front gates.

Stepping into the grand foyer, the senior housekeeper approached with a gentle bow.

"Oh dear, President Kang... that was your favorite shirt. Shall I soak out the blood?"

"No need. Burn it."

His tone was utterly indifferent. Was the corpse one of Chairman Kang’s lieutenants? Before Jakyeong could ask, Il-hyun vanished upstairs to shower.

Turning back toward the salon, Jakyeong’s eyes snagged on two figures seated on the leather sectional.

They weren't domestic staff.

Dressed in identical dark suits, the men sat with unnatural, rigid posture, staring straight ahead like living statues—eerily reminiscent of the silicone mannequin upstairs. Their exposed forearms and necks bore fine combat lacerations, and one man was missing his left pinky finger.

The man wearing dark sunglasses slowly turned his head, fixing his gaze on Jakyeong.

Though his eyes were hidden, the thick, metallic stench of fresh blood rolling off him was suffocating.

Jakyeong’s instincts flared instantly: Contract killers.

They were cut from the exact same cloth as him.
